phase3_findings.description: Wrong-type guard covers JSON objects (the [object Object] sentinel, matched as a substring so mixed arrays are caught) but not a top-level JSON scalar non-string: a config value that is a bool/number is coerced by config-get.sh to 'true'/'false'/'42', passes the object guard, and is applied verbatim as a garbage label reported 'applied'. Bounded impact (a visibly-odd but valid label on an internal provenance channel); the #1855 test block explicitly documents this scalar row as out-of-scope, so it is a design-accepted residual.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: wrong-type-guard-gap: scalar-non-string config value applied as a label

phase3_findings.description: Config-driven mode wins unconditionally over positional labels: if a caller passes both positional labels and --config-key, the positionals are silently dropped with no breadcrumb. No current call site mixes the two, so latent only.

phase3_findings.description: OUTCOME CONTRACT docstring at apply-labels.sh:31 says 'config-unreadable — --config-key mode and config-get exited non-zero', but the same token is also emitted on the wrong-type path (lines 102-105) where config-get exits 0 and the [object Object] sentinel is detected. The closed-set summary under-describes one producer of the token.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: docstring-accuracy: contract enumeration omits the wrong-type producer of config-unreadable

phase3_findings.description: The folded per-label ensure-label.sh creation loop (apply-labels.sh:159-161) — the headline new behavior — is only covered transitively; no assertion verifies each normalized label is actually passed to ensure-label.sh. A regression dropping the loop, mis-quoting a multi-word label, or passing wrong label text would still print 'applied' and stay green. A stub ensure-label.sh recording its argv would close it. (Also minor: api-failure untested in config-driven mode; config-unreadable via missing-python3 rc-2 not independently asserted — both functionally covered by shared code paths.)
phase3_findings.defect_signature: test-gap: folded label-creation loop only indirectly covered

phase4_report:
Phase 4.1 report (inline): PR #1936 (issue #1855) folds label config-resolution and outcome classification into scripts/apply-labels.sh — a new --config-key/--config-fallback config-driven mode (the helper resolves the label list itself via config-get.sh), a folded per-label ensure-label.sh creation step, and a closed 5-token stdout outcome contract {applied, nothing-to-apply, arg-slip, api-failure, config-unreadable} so call sites route on a token rather than English stderr sentences. scripts/ensure-label.sh replaces grep -qiE already-exists classification with a bash case under shopt -s nocasematch (grep-less-host portability). Four implement-skill label call sites collapse from a config-get read + per-label ensure + apply into a single apply-labels.sh call each; stale prose is corrected; and a thorough #1855 behavioral test block (all five tokens, the full six-shape config adversarial matrix, mixed-array substring guard, case-insensitive and grep-less already-exists arms) replaces the retired hand-copied deferred_labels_normalize() mirror.

Strengths: the core helper is correct and internally consistent (number shifted off before flag parsing; every path emits exactly one token before exit 0; set -uo pipefail with no set -e preserves the always-exit-0 contract; gh POST stdout -> /dev/null keeps the token channel clean; label normalization is bash-builtins-only per CLAUDE.md guard-class 2). config-get.sh coupling is sound (object substring guard catches mixed arrays; rc!=0 routes to config-unreadable, never a silent empty set). Backward compatibility of positional call sites is preserved. Test coverage is behavioral and strong. Both prior fix iterations landed on-branch and the monolith shard is GREEN.

Verdict rationale: one Important finding — the canonical mechanism doc docs/internal/implement-skill.md (which CLAUDE.md names as the disclosure surface) still describes the retired per-phase config-get/normalize/ensure mechanism at lines 1500-1513 and 1768-1777, a coupled-mirror the change was required to update in the same commit; leaving it would misdirect a maintainer or autonomous run to reintroduce the exact idiom this PR removed (and which the new run.sh absence-pins now turn RED). DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md:892 is a related, lesser incomplete-mirror. Remaining findings are Suggestions (design-accepted scalar-config residual, config-mode-vs-positional precedence, a docstring accuracy gap, and a folded-creation-loop test gap). REJECT pending the coupled-mirror doc update; the code and tests themselves are merge-ready.
